title: SD Basic Functions and Procedure Matrix
purpose: Compare similar-looking SD procedures without pretending they all use the same engine.

rows.assignment_anchor: Customer master/account group, sales document type, and item category depending on partner object.
rows.engine: Partner functions, source control, and master relationships
rows.managed_data: Business partner/customer relationships and document partners
rows.trace: Procedure assignment → partner function → mandatory/changeable flag → source control → master relationship
rows.redetermination_note: Changing document or partner context can change the partner set; prove source control before downstream debugging.

rows.assignment_anchor: Text object level such as sales document header or item category.
rows.engine: Text types plus ordered source search
rows.access_sequence: Yes, but this is a text-source access sequence rather than pricing condition technique
rows.managed_data: Master texts, predecessor texts, and standard texts
rows.trace: Procedure assignment → text type → access sequence → first valid source → copy/reference behavior
rows.redetermination_note: A follow-on document can copy old predecessor text or search a source again depending on the text rules.

rows.assignment_anchor: Sales area + customer pricing procedure + document pricing procedure determine the pricing procedure.
rows.access_sequence: Yes, per condition type where automatic record search is required
rows.managed_data: Prices, discounts, surcharges, tax, and other condition records
rows.trace: Procedure determination → condition type → access sequence → key → validity → requirement/formula
rows.redetermination_note: Copy control and document-type changes can cause repricing. Prove the pricing type and procedure before changing records.

rows.managed_data: Material substitution and product-selection condition records
rows.trace: Document type → procedure → condition type → access sequence → condition record → substitution reason
rows.redetermination_note: If the material-determination procedure changes with the document type, material determination is run again.

rows.assignment_anchor: Activated for the relevant sales-document context and evaluated against customer/material condition records.
rows.engine: Condition-technique record search plus allow/block check
rows.access_sequence: yes where configured for the listing/exclusion condition type
rows.trace: Procedure/context → condition type/access → customer/material key → validity → allow/block result
rows.redetermination_note: A changed document type can cause listing/exclusion to be checked again when its procedure differs.

rows.assignment_anchor: Sales-order commercial context plus free-goods configuration and valid master record.
rows.engine: Free-goods agreement search and quantity qualification
rows.access_sequence: Uses condition-technique concepts in classic SD free-goods design
rows.managed_data: Free-goods agreements, thresholds, and inclusive/exclusive rules
rows.trace: Process support → agreement validity → quantity threshold → free-goods rule → generated subitem
rows.redetermination_note: A changed document type can cause free-goods determination to run again when its procedure differs.

rows.assignment_anchor: Sales document type and item category; other document-control levels can participate by process.
rows.engine: Configured required fields plus status effects
rows.trace: Procedure assignment → missing field → status group → affected follow-on processing
rows.redetermination_note: Completeness changes when a controlled field is filled, cleared, or changed; the important result is the follow-on status.

rows.assignment_anchor: Framework-specific: classic SD output procedures are assigned to document context; S/4HANA Output Control uses output parameter rules.
rows.engine: Classic condition technique or modern rule/decision-table evaluation
rows.access_sequence: Classic: yes where output conditions are used. Modern Output Control: rule-based parameter determination.
rows.managed_data: Output conditions or output rules, recipients, channels, forms, and dispatch parameters
rows.trace: First identify framework → output item → successful rule/condition → recipient → channel → form → dispatch status
rows.redetermination_note: Do not mix NAST-style output analysis with S/4HANA Output Control analysis.

rows.assignment_anchor: Customer procedure + document procedure + product-proposal procedure determination.
rows.engine: Ordered access to proposal data sources
rows.managed_data: Order history, listing/exclusion, item proposals, customer-material records, and customer-specific sources
rows.trace: Customer/document procedure → proposal procedure → source order → proposal result → user acceptance
rows.redetermination_note: Standard sales checks start after the user accepts a proposal and enters order quantity.
